questions.title: Two Integer Arithmetic Drill
questions.description:
You are practicing the five basic arithmetic operations. Read two integers and apply all of them.

Input Format:
One line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
Print five lines, in order: the sum a + b, the difference a - b, the product a * b, the integer quotient a / b, and the remainder a % b.

Constraints:
1 <= a, b <= 10000; division is integer division, so the quotient is truncated.

questions.title: Compare Two Integers
questions.description:
Practice every relational operator on a pair of integers. Note that Java prints booleans in lowercase.

Input Format:
One line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
Print six lines (lowercase true or false): the result of a < b, then a > b, a <= b, a >= b, a == b, and a != b.

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 100000.

questions.title: Compound Assignment Sequence
questions.description:
Watch how compound assignment operators change a variable step by step. Start with n and apply the sequence below using m, printing n after every step.

Input Format:
One line with two space-separated integers n and m.

Output Format:
Print five lines: n after n += m, then after n *= 2, then after n -= m, then after n /= 3, and finally after n %= 7.

Constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 1000; /= and %= are integer operations.

questions.title: Bitwise Playground
questions.description:
Explore the bitwise operators on two non-negative integers.

Input Format:
One line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
Print six lines: a & b, then a | b, then a ^ b, then ~a, then a << 1, and finally a >> 1.

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 100000.

questions.title: Increment Decrement Trace
questions.description:
Trace pre-increment, post-increment, pre-decrement and post-decrement on two variables. The postfix forms yield the old value; the prefix forms yield the new value.

Input Format:
One line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
Let x start as a and y start as b. Print five lines: the value of x++, then ++x, then y--, then --y, and finally x + y.

Constraints:
1 <= a, b <= 100.

questions.title: Precedence Evaluation Drill
questions.description:
Java evaluates *, / and % before + and -, and parentheses override everything. Check six precedence-heavy expressions on three integers.

Input Format:
One line with three space-separated integers a, b and c.

Output Format:
Print six lines: a + b * c, then (a + b) * c, then a - b / c, then (a - b) / c, then a * b % c, and finally a + b % c, each evaluated with normal Java precedence.

Constraints:
1 <= a, b, c <= 100.

questions.title: Trip Expense Splitter
questions.description:
Four friends went on a trek and paid one total bill. They split the cost equally; whatever cannot be divided evenly stays as leftover rupees.

Input Format:
One line with two space-separated integers: the total cost in rupees and the number of friends.

Output Format:
Print two lines: 'Each pays: X' where X is the integer share per friend, then 'Left over: Y' where Y is the remaining rupees.

Constraints:
1 <= cost <= 1000000 and 1 <= friends <= 100.

questions.title: Festival Discount Calculator
questions.description:
During a festival sale a shop gives a flat percentage discount. Purchases of at least 5000 rupees get 20 percent off, everything else gets 10 percent off. The discount is computed with integer arithmetic and truncated.

Input Format:
One line with a single integer amount.

Output Format:
Print one line: 'Final price: X' where X is amount minus the truncated discount, choosing the percentage with a ternary expression.

Constraints:
1 <= amount <= 100000.

questions.title: Mystery Box Type Checker
questions.description:
A warehouse scanner reads a tag and a value, then packs the value into an Object box. Depending on the tag, the value is stored as a String (a word), an Integer (a whole number) or a Double (a decimal number). Report what kind of object ended up in the box using instanceof.

Input Format:
One line: a tag (text, count or price) followed by one value. For text the value is a single word without spaces; for count it is an integer; for price it is a decimal number.

Output Format:
Print three lines (lowercase true or false): box instanceof String, then box instanceof Integer, then box instanceof Double.

Constraints:
tag is exactly one of: text, count, price.
questions.inputconstrains: tag is one of: text, count, price

questions.title: Celsius to Fahrenheit Converter
questions.description:
A weather app converts Celsius to Fahrenheit. Besides the exact value it also shows the whole-degree mark obtained with an explicit (int) cast.

Input Format:
One line with a single decimal number celsius.

Output Format:
Line 1: 'Fahrenheit: X' with X printed to exactly 2 decimals, where F = C * 9 / 5 + 32. Line 2: 'Whole degrees: N' where N is (int) F.

Constraints:
-50.0 <= celsius <= 150.0.

questions.title: Leap Year Checker
questions.description:
Every February 29 the calendar team re-checks the leap year rule: a year is leap if it is divisible by 400, or divisible by 4 but not by 100. Decide using the logical operators || and &&.

Input Format:
One line with a single integer year.

Output Format:
Print a single line, lowercase true or false.

Constraints:
1 <= year <= 3000.

questions.title: Permission Flags Checker
questions.description:
A server stores user rights as an 8-bit permission mask. Given two users' masks, report the rights they share, the rights anyone holds, and the rights only the first user has. Use the bitwise operators & and | (with ~ for the complement).

Input Format:
One line with two space-separated integers p1 and p2.

Output Format:
Print three lines: 'Shared: X' where X = p1 & p2, then 'Combined: Y' where Y = p1 | p2, then 'Only in first: Z' where Z = p1 & ~p2.

Constraints:
0 <= p1, p2 <= 255.

questions.title: Grade From Marks Ternary Chain
questions.description:
An exam portal maps marks to letter grades with a single nested ternary expression (if statements are forbidden): 90 or above is A, 75 to 89 is B, 60 to 74 is C, 40 to 59 is D, below 40 is F.

Input Format:
One line with a single integer marks.

Output Format:
Print the single letter grade.

Constraints:
0 <= marks <= 100.

questions.title: Meter to Feet and Inches Converter
questions.description:
A travel app converts metres for hikers. It reports the complete feet (truncated with an explicit (int) cast) plus the leftover inches, using 1 metre = 3.28084 feet.

Input Format:
One line with a single decimal number meters.

Output Format:
Line 1: 'Feet: N' where N is the integer part of meters * 3.28084 obtained by an (int) cast. Line 2: 'Inches: X' where X is the remaining (totalFeet - feet) * 12 printed to exactly 2 decimals.

Constraints:
0 <= meters <= 100.

questions.title: XOR Swap Without Extra Variable
questions.description:
Old-school programmers swapped two variables without any extra variable using only the XOR operator. Demonstrate the trick: apply a ^= b, then b ^= a, then a ^= b.

Input Format:
One line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
Print two lines after the swap: 'First: X' holding the original b, then 'Second: Y' holding the original a.

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 100000.

questions.title: Electricity Bill Slab Calculator
questions.description:
A city bills electricity in slabs: the first 100 units cost 3.50 per unit, the next 100 units cost 5.00 per unit, and every unit above 200 costs 8.00 per unit. Accumulate the bill with compound assignment using relational comparisons.

Input Format:
One line with a single integer units.

Output Format:
Print one line: the bill amount to exactly 2 decimals.

Constraints:
0 <= units <= 5000.

questions.title: Set Bits and Highest Position
questions.description:
A debugging toolbox inspects the bits of a number. For the given non-negative integer report how many bits are set, the position of the highest set bit (0-indexed; use -1 when the number is 0), and whether the number is an exact power of two. Use the unsigned right shift >>> to walk the bits.

Input Format:
One line with a single integer n.

Output Format:
Three lines: 'Set bits: X', then 'Highest position: Y', then 'Power of two: Z' where Z is lowercase true or false.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 1000000000.

questions.title: Salary Bonus With Nested Ternaries
questions.description:
A company pays an annual bonus decided by rating and service years, coded as one nested ternary expression (if statements are forbidden): rating 1 earns 20 percent for 5 or more years of service, otherwise 15 percent; rating 2 earns 12 percent for 5 or more years, otherwise 8 percent; rating 3 always earns 5 percent. Also report the truncated whole-rupee monthly hike.

Input Format:
One line: salary (decimal number), years (integer) and rating (1 to 3), space separated.

Output Format:
Line 1: 'Bonus: X' with X to exactly 2 decimals. Line 2: 'New salary: Y' with Y to exactly 2 decimals. Line 3: 'Monthly hike: N' where N is (int) (bonus / 12).

Constraints:
1000 <= salary <= 1000000; 0 <= years <= 40; rating is 1, 2 or 3.

questions.title: Decimal to Binary via Shifts
questions.description:
A low-level tool shows a number in base 2 without using Integer.toBinaryString: it starts from a single 1-bit flag shifted left until it sits above the highest set bit, then walks the flag down while printing one bit at a time. It also previews two shift results.

Input Format:
One line with a single integer n.

Output Format:
Line 1: 'Binary: B' with no leading zeros (just 0 when n is 0). Line 2: 'Doubled: X' which is n << 1. Line 3: 'Halved: Y' which is n >> 1.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 1000000000.

questions.title: Fast Power Modulo Calculator
questions.description:
Cryptographic routines raise huge powers but only need the remainder. Compute base raised to exponent modulo m using fast modular exponentiation (square-and-multiply) in a while loop. Remember that in Java the * operator binds tighter than %, so result * base % m means (result * base) % m.

Input Format:
One line with three space-separated integers: base, exponent and modulus.

Output Format:
Print one line: base raised to exponent, modulo modulus.

Constraints:
1 <= base <= 2000000000; 0 <= exponent <= 1000000000; 1 <= modulus <= 2000000000.
